targets.title: Repeated testing produces superior transfer of learning relative to repeated studying.
targets.evidence_quote: The first experiment of the present study was a direct replication of Butler’s third experiment.
targets.outcome_quote:
Taken together, the current study shows that the testing effect in far transfer across different knowledge domains (
Butler, 2010
) is robust. We replicated the results of
Butler’s (2010)
third experiment with a comparable effect size, indicating that retrieval practice can greatly enhance performance on a far transfer test.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly conclude that the effect is robust and replicated. Their additional exposure-control condition reduces but does not eliminate the retrieval advantage; they do not judge the test invalid.

reasoning: Identity verified against title, DOI, and four authors. Both new experiments test Butler’s third experiment; other retrieval-practice studies serve background roles. Overall authors’ verdict governs despite the mechanistic qualification.
